verdict: In its first full quarter as a standalone company, FedEx Freight grew revenue 8.1% to $2.4 billion, but $105 million of separation costs held operating income to $253 million and net income to $147 million.

segments.name: Less-than-truckload freight
segments.note: FedEx Freight is a single-segment business: less-than-truckload (LTL) trucking — many customers' pallets sharing each trailer — across North America.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear-and-tear on tractors, trailers, terminals and systems.

opex.name: Separation & other costs
opex.note: One-off costs of splitting from FedEx and standing up as an independent public company.

opex.name: Insurance & claims
opex.note: Accident and cargo claims and the insurance behind them — a real cost of running trucks.

opex.name: Operating taxes & licenses
opex.note: Licenses and non-income taxes on operations.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $55M on the debt taken on at separation, partly offset by $5M of interest income and $1M of other income — a net $49M cost. A year ago this line instead held $98M of interest income from FedEx, its then-parent.
follow100Note: Direct operating costs = salaries & employee benefits ($1,128M) + operating supplies & expenses ($546M) + purchased transportation ($235M), the FedEx Freight expense lines that move directly with shipments.

takeaways.title: Growth in a soft freight market
takeaways.text: Three-month revenue rose to $2,442M from $2,259M a year ago (when the business was still inside FedEx), helped by pricing and fuel surcharges even as daily shipments softened.

takeaways.title: Separation is not free
takeaways.text: Separation and other costs of $105M in the quarter cut GAAP operating income to $253M from $290M a year ago. On the four-month view the company headlines, adjusted operating income was $510M, up 16.4%.

takeaways.title: A new standalone baseline
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.98 vs $1.95 a year ago under FedEx — the drop mostly reflects separation costs, new standalone interest expense, and losing the old parent-company interest income.

oneTimers: This page covers the three months ended September 30, 2026 from FedEx Freight's own Form 10-Q. Its earnings release headlined a one-time four-month transition period (June 1–September 30, 2026, including its last month inside the old fiscal calendar): revenue $3,281M, GAAP operating income $383M, net income $230M, adjusted EPS $2.15.
FedEx Freight became independent on June 1, 2026 and moved its year-end to December 31; prior-year figures are carve-out results from when it was a FedEx segment, so comparisons are approximate.

sources.label: Official earnings release for the transition period (SEC EDGAR Form 8-K Ex. 99.1)
Form 10-Q with the three-month statements (SEC EDGAR)

footerNote: FedEx Freight reports one list of operating expenses with no gross-profit line; salaries, operating supplies and purchased transportation are shown as direct operating costs and the rest as running costs, so the chart keeps the standard shape. It is a single reportable segment (LTL freight).
